Subject: Stakeholder mapping & buying process - Acme Corp

Alex  great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from today's discovery call so we have alignment as you map stakeholders:

- Decision criteria (what you told us): 1) latency <= 200ms p95 for chat features, 2) strict data residency and audit logs, 3) ability to run on dedicated capacity with VPC peering, 4) clear unit economics/forecasting for scale.
- Economic buyer: you indicated CTO-level sign-off (Matt Raines), but Procurement will own commercial terms.
- Security/legal: Maya Singh (security) + Legal (TBD) will validate SOC2/audit artifacts and data retention controls.
- Procurement steps: standard MSA + SOW, potential need for 60-day invoice terms and an SLA exception.

As discussed, two asks for your team: (1) Can you confirm the full stakeholder list with emails for procurement, security, legal, and the economic buyer? (2) Can you share any mandatory contract language or internal redlines up front so we can triage?

Internal note: I'm attaching the proposed pricing term sheet and the security questionnaire we typically send to customers (attached).

Attachments: pricing_term_sheet.xlsx (12 KB), security_questionnaire.pdf (45 KB)

Next steps:
- Alex to share stakeholders and procurement process by EOD tomorrow.
- I'll loop in Sales Ops and Legal if they need to review exceptions.

Thanks  Marissa

Thanks Marissa  good recap. Confirming stakeholders below:

- Matt Raines (CTO / economic buyer)  matt.raines@acme.com
- Priya Kapoor (Head of Procurement)  procurement@acme.com (primary contact)
- Maya Singh (Security lead)  maya.singh@acme.com
- Legal: contracts@acme.com (will loop Legal once Procurement flags specific clauses)

Procurement notes:
- Standard timeline: procurement review (1 week) -> legal redlines (up to 2 weeks) -> exec sign-off.
- We can consider a 5% onboarding discount for multi-year commitments, but invoice terms are usually Net 30; 60-day terms require senior approval.
- SLA exceptions: Security needs to review controls before we can approve any deviation.

I'll upload our standard procurement checklist to you and can connect our procurement lead with your CS/Legal if needed.

Forwarding Acme's stakeholder list and procurement notes. Procurement may ask for: 1) 60-day invoice terms, 2) an upfront onboarding discount (~5%), and 3) an SLA exception contingent on security review.

Ask: can Sales Ops / Revenue approve the discount and invoice-term exception so I can respond to Procurement quickly? If not, what is the escalation path?

Context: deal is healthy, expected ARR $780k first year. Economic buyer is CTO Matt Raines. Security will need the SOC2 artifacts and audit logs (we have those ready).

Attachments: pricing_term_sheet.xlsx, security_questionnaire.pdf

Suggested guardrails: approve up to 5% discount without Legal signoff; invoice-term exceptions (Net60) require Finance approval but Sales leadership could pre-authorize escalation for strategic deals.

Thanks  Marissa
